newsitem.title: UK: Texaco gets UK approval to develop Galley.
newsitem.headline: Texaco gets UK approval to develop Galley.

text.p: U.S. oil major Texaco Inc said on Wednesday it had received British government approval to develop the Galley oil and gas field in the central North Sea.
First oil from Galley should flow in the first quarter of 1998, peaking at 43,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
Texaco North Sea is operator of the field and owns 67.4 percent. Enterprise Oil owns 17.4 percent and Lasmo the remaining 15.2 percent.
Estimated recoverable reserves are 28 million barrels of oil and 40 billion cubic feet of gas, Texaco said.

Galley, which lies in block 15/23a of the British North Sea some 145 km ortheast of the Scottish town of Peterhead, will be developed using a floating production facility (FPF) -- the Northern Producer -- leased from Seatankers for a minimum of four years.

Full production processing will be carried out on the Northern Producer, which was previously used as an FPF on Midland and Scottish Energy's Emerald field, before oil is pumped to the Flotta terminal in the Orkney Islands.

Oil production is expected to peak at about 35,000 barrels per day. Gas, which will be piped to the St. Fergus terminal in northeast Scotland, should flow at a peak rate of 50 million cubic feet per day.
